articles.title: Retired Officer Snubbed, UP Power Official Boasts Political Links in Audio
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Basti, UP – A retired officer, upset over frequent power cuts, called a local electricity department official to register a complaint. Instead of addressing the issue, the officer asked him to call the 1912 helpline.

body.html:
Basti, UP – A retired officer, upset over frequent power cuts, called a local electricity department official to register a complaint. Instead of addressing the issue, the officer asked him to call the 1912 helpline.

When the complainant identified himself as a retired officer, the official responded arrogantly, boasting about his connections with top leaders including Union Minister SP Singh Baghel, former Governor Baby Rani Maurya, Raj Babbar, and Rajya Sabha MP Ramjilal Suman.

The audio of this exchange has now been made public by UP’s Power Minister AK Sharma, drawing sharp criticism for the officer's conduct.

articles.title: Kanpur Station Chaos: TTE Beats Passenger, Gets Thrashed in Return—Video Goes Viral!
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Kanpur, UP – Tension erupted at Kanpur Central Railway Station on Tuesday when a scuffle between a Train Ticket Examiner (TTE) and a group of passengers turned violent. The incident was caught on camera and has gone viral on social media.

body.html:
Kanpur, UP – Tension erupted at Kanpur Central Railway Station on Tuesday when a scuffle between a Train Ticket Examiner (TTE) and a group of passengers turned violent. The incident was caught on camera and has gone viral on social media.

According to reports, 15–20 youths travelling on a special train from Surat to Muzaffarpur allegedly barged into the ladies’ coach. When the TTE intervened, a heated argument broke out. Matters escalated when the TTE dragged one of the youths off the train and began beating him on the platform.

Seeing this, fellow passengers tried to stop the TTE. When he didn’t relent, they retaliated and assaulted the TTE. In one video, the TTE is seen slapping a man whose shirt is torn. In another, angry men pin the TTE to the ground and pull his hair.

The Railway Protection Force (RPF) later arrived and detained one passenger, Raja Yadav. No action has been taken so far against the TTEs involved.

articles.title: Indore SI Caught at Woman’s House, Beaten by Locals—Dragged, Stripped, and Tied to Pole!
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Indore, MP – Sub-Inspector Suresh Bunkar was severely thrashed by a group of women in the Khajrana area around 6 AM on Thursday (24.07.2025). Locals used sticks to beat him, attempted to tie him to an electric pole, and even tried to strip him.

body.html:
Indore, MP – Sub-Inspector Suresh Bunkar was severely thrashed by a group of women in the Khajrana area around 6 AM on Thursday (24.07.2025). Locals used sticks to beat him, attempted to tie him to an electric pole, and even tried to strip him.

Reports say Bunkar was found at a woman’s house in the Khedi area. The woman is reportedly in a marital dispute. SI Bunkar, who came into contact with her during this time, had been visiting her home for the past two months. On Thursday, her family and neighbours caught him there.

Eyewitnesses allege that Bunkar was drunk and misbehaving, which triggered the violent reaction from the public. Khajrana police reached the spot but failed to control the crowd. Additional force from Palasia had to be called in to rescue the officer. Some women have been detained, and four individuals have been booked for attempt to murder.

SI Bunkar has a controversial past. Two years ago, he was beaten by youths in the Lasudia area while intoxicated on duty. The incident had led to serious injuries and a public parade of the accused by police.

articles.title: Ahmedabad Schoolgirl Jumps to Death from 4th Floor — No Signs of Stress, Yet No One Knew Why
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Ahmedabad: A tragic incident has shaken the city as a Class 10 student of a reputed school in Navrangpura ended her life by jumping from the fourth floor of the school building during the break on Thursday.

body.html:
Ahmedabad: A tragic incident has shaken the city as a Class 10 student of a reputed school in Navrangpura ended her life by jumping from the fourth floor of the school building during the break on Thursday.

The 16-year-old student reportedly appeared cheerful and normal before the incident. She was rushed to the hospital after sustaining severe injuries, but doctors could not save her.

According to classmates and teachers, the girl was good in academics and showed no signs of mental stress. A classmate said she was joking in class before the break.

The Ahmedabad crime branch has taken over the investigation. Police have seized the student’s mobile phone and are analysing her call records, chats, and social media activity. CCTV footage is being reviewed, and statements from family, friends, and teachers are being recorded. The girl's family suspects she may have been under mental pressure or facing harassment, and they have demanded a fair and transparent probe.

Child psychiatrist Dr. Sandeep Rawal said rising academic pressure, social media exposure, and lack of emotional support often push students to breaking points. He emphasised the need for schools and parents to build open channels for children to express their issues.

Initial inquiry reveals serious security lapses in the school. The fourth-floor balcony lacked a safety grill or net, and there was no counselling support for students.

The education department has now ordered a review of the school’s safety measures. The incident has raised pressing concerns about the mental well-being of students and the accountability of institutions.

articles.title: We Won’t Pay, Do Whatever You Can!’: Mirzapur Cop Caught on Video Threatening Shopkeeper Over ₹800
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Mirzapur: A controversy erupted in Ramai Patti market under the City Kotwali police station area on Friday after a police inspector, allegedly in uniform, refused to pay ₹800 for a pair of repaired spectacles.

body.html:
Mirzapur: A controversy erupted in Ramai Patti market under the City Kotwali police station area on Friday after a police inspector, allegedly in uniform, refused to pay ₹800 for a pair of repaired spectacles.

According to the shopkeeper, the officer had his lenses fitted and was presented with the bill. When asked for payment, the officer reportedly said, “We won’t pay. Do whatever you can,” in an arrogant tone. The shopkeeper requested him to speak politely, but the officer left the shop without paying.

A video of the incident quickly went viral on local WhatsApp groups and social media, sparking public outrage.

Authorities have directed the city police to verify the facts and take appropriate action in the matter.

articles.title: Man Gets Non-Veg Soup Instead of Veg, Responds Calmly  But Netizens Lash Out at His 'Chill' Reaction
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: New Delhi: A post on X (formerly Twitter) by a user has gone viral after he shared his calm response to receiving the wrong food order. Shekhar Dutt, a teacher as per his bio, claimed he ordered a vegetarian soup but was delivered a non-vegetarian one via Zomato.

body.html:
New Delhi: A post on X (formerly Twitter) by a user has gone viral after he shared his calm response to receiving the wrong food order. Shekhar Dutt, a teacher as per his bio, claimed he ordered a vegetarian soup but was delivered a non-vegetarian one via Zomato.

Instead of creating chaos, he filed a complaint on the app. Zomato promptly apologised and issued a full refund. Sharing a video of the soup, he wrote:
"We ordered veg soup from a premium restaurant. We were delivered non-veg soup. No, we didn’t create any ruckus. We complained to Zomato and they issued a prompt apology and refund. Mistakes can happen anywhere. Let’s not make them larger than life."

While some appreciated his maturity, a majority of netizens criticised his soft stance, arguing that food preferences — especially vegetarian or religious-based — are serious matters and shouldn’t be taken lightly.

The post has sparked a debate online over how such food delivery errors should be handled.

articles.title: Tragedy in Naigaon: 4-Year-Old Falls from 12th Floor — CCTV Captures Heartbreaking Final Moments
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Naigaon (Vasai East): A heartbreaking incident took place on Tuesday night at Navkar Phase-1, a 14-storey residential complex in Naigaon East, where a 4-year-old girl, Anvika Prajapati, fell to her death from the 12th floor.

body.html:
Naigaon (Vasai East): A heartbreaking incident took place on Tuesday night at Navkar Phase-1, a 14-storey residential complex in Naigaon East, where a 4-year-old girl, Anvika Prajapati, fell to her death from the 12th floor.

According to reports, Anvika had gone to her sister’s home and was preparing to leave when the tragedy occurred. While playing, she climbed onto a wooden stand near the window, which had no safety grill or net. The structure collapsed under her weight, causing her to fall.

The incident was captured on CCTV and the footage has since gone viral on social media. Residents rushed the child to Vasai-Virar Municipal Hospital, but she was declared dead on arrival.

The local police have registered a case of accidental death and have launched an investigation. They have also emphasized the urgent need for safety precautions in high-rise buildings, especially in areas accessible to children.

The Naigaon community is in mourning, and the tragic death has raised serious questions about child safety in residential complexes.

articles.title: Worm in Pongal or ₹25 Lakh Extortion Plot? Bengaluru’s Rameshwaram Cafe Calls Viral Video a Setup!
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bengaluru: A controversy erupted at Rameshwaram Café's Bengaluru airport outlet on Thursday morning after a group of customers alleged they found a worm in their dish.

body.html:
Bengaluru: A controversy erupted at Rameshwaram Café's Bengaluru airport outlet on Thursday morning after a group of customers alleged they found a worm in their dish. The video of the incident, showing a man pointing at a worm in his spoon and speaking of a complaint, has gone viral online.

The cafe staff immediately apologised and refunded ₹300. However, the restaurant has now claimed the entire scene was staged to extort ₹25 lakh and malign their brand.

In a statement issued Thursday evening, Rameshwaram Café called the allegation false and submitted call logs, message screenshots, and related evidence to the police, demanding legal action.

Founder Divya Raghav said, “We categorically deny the baseless accusation. This was a malicious attempt to damage our reputation. We maintain the highest hygiene standards, especially at airport locations.”

Notably, the chain had earlier faced scrutiny in May 2024 when expired items were found at its Hyderabad outlet.

articles.title: "‘Why Pay for Another Man’s Child?’: Court Sparks Debate on Illegitimate Child's Right
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a recent case, a court witnessed a heated exchange after a DNA report confirmed that a man was not the biological father of a child. During the proceedings, the man's lawyer questioned whether illegitimate children have the right to maintenance under Section 125 of the CrPC.

body.html:
In a recent case, a court witnessed a heated exchange after a DNA report confirmed that a man was not the biological father of a child. During the proceedings, the man's lawyer questioned whether illegitimate children have the right to maintenance under Section 125 of the CrPC.

The judge responded affirmatively, saying, “Yes, yes.” However, the man argued, “Why should I pay for someone else’s child? The woman who cheated and the man who fathered the child should be held responsible.”

The case has sparked debate around legal obligations, paternity fraud, and the interpretation of maintenance laws under Indian jurisprudence.
